For Respondent No.3 : Ms. Sunita Jain, Advocate on behalf of Ms. M. Asha, Advocate.
Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on board 14.02.2024 1.

This is claimants appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, MV Act)
against the award dated 28.01.2020 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhamtari (in short, the Tribunal) in Claim Case No.56/2018, whereby the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.7,10,400/- to the appellants/claimants on account of death of son of appellant No.1/claimant No.1 and brother of appellant No.2/claimant No.2, namely, Sanjay Kumar Sahu in a motor accident took place on 27.12.2017 by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle crane bearing registration No.CG-05 G-8518, driven by respondent No.1 Dharmendra Kumar Rajbhar,
owned by respondent No.2 Sudha Ram and insured by respondent No.3, the Oriental Insurance Company Limited.
2. As per the pleadings, deceased Sanjay Kumar Sahu was working as mason and was earning Rs.9,000/- per month.
The appellants/claimants were dependent upon the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: 3. The respondents No.1 and 2 contested the claim of the claimants before the Tribunal by filing their written statement and submitted in it that the deceased himself was negligent in accident and he was driving his motorcycle in rashly and negligently.

The respondent No.1, driver of the offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and if any amount of compensation is being determined, the liability to pay is upon the insurance company as there is no breach of policy condition.

4. The respondent No.3 has also contested the claim before the Tribunal and filed its written statement separately and pleaded that at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not having any effective and valid driving licence and offending vehicle was being driven in violation of policy condition.
It was also pleaded in the written statement that the deceased himself is liable for contributory negligence as he was driving his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner.

5. On the basis of pleadings, the learned Tribunal has framed six issues and after appreciating the evidence available on record, decided the claim in favour of the appellants/claimants and the Tribunal found that monthly income of the deceased was Rs.4500/- per month and awarded the compensation amount accordingly.
6.

Mr. Praveen K. Dhurandhar, learned counsel for the appellants would submit that deceased Sanjay Kumar Sahu was a Mason aged about 22 years and he was skilled labour and therefore, the income of the deceased ought to have been considered by the learned Tribunal as Rs.9000/- per month as claimed by the claimants.
In alternative, he submits that looking to the date of accident at least minimum wages prescribed should have been taken for assessment of the compensation amount.
He would further submit that the amount awarded towards pecuniary and non-pecuniary heads are also on lower side and the same may also be enhanced suitably.

7. On the other hand, Mr. Kunal Das, learned counsel for the respondents No.1 and 2 has supported the impugned award passed by the claims Tribunal and has submitted that any amount awarded by the Tribunal or enhanced by this Hon'ble Court, the liability to pay such amount is upon the insurance company as there is no breach of any policy condition.

8. The counsel for respondent No.3 insurance company would also support the impugned award passed by the Tribunal and has submitted that there is no document submitted by the claimants with respect to the income of the deceased and in absence of that the Tribunal has rightly considered the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4500/- and the amount awarded in other heads are also justified and therefore, the impugned award need not be interfered with and the claimants are not entitled for any enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the claims Tribunal.
9. I have heard the counsel for the parties, considered their submissions and perused the records.

10. Barring the oral evidence of the appellants/claimants no document with regard to proof/income of the deceased has been filed, however, looking to nature of job on the date of accident and minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident, this Court is of the view that Rs.8000/- can safely be taken as income of the deceased on the date of accident.

12.
For the forgoing reason, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.7,10,400/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.13,19,600/-.
Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs.7,10,400/-, the claimants are entitled for an additional amount of Rs.6,09,200/-.
The additional amount shall carry interest @ 6 percent per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated hereinabove.
13. The insurance company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from today.

On such deposit being made, Rs.4,00,000/- shall be deposited in the name of appellants (Rs.2,00,000/- for each appellant) for a period of five years in FDR at any nationalized Bank and the remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
14. With the above observations this appeal is partly allowed.
